about.title: Los Altos Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Santa Clara County recorded 40 injury collisions and 1 traffic death in Los Altos during the most recent final crash year, with Thursday mornings between 8 and 10 a.m. showing the heaviest concentration of reported crashes. Behind each number is a family left to sort through grief, funeral arrangements, and unanswered questions about how a loved one's life ended. California law recognizes that a spouse, domestic partner, or children may bring a wrongful death claim, and if none exist, certain other dependents or heirs may qualify. These claims are separate from any criminal case that might follow the same incident and focus instead on compensating the family for what was lost. Our team can explain standing, deadlines, and what losses may be recoverable, all at no upfront fee.

whyChoose.title: Why Los Altos Families Choose Us

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, then to certain other dependents or heirs if none exist. We can help sort out who in your family qualifies before any claim moves forward.

items.title: A Firm Two-Year Window
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, though claims involving a government entity carry a much shorter deadline. Given the corridors and intersections in Los Altos where public agencies sometimes share responsibility, getting timely legal guidance matters.

items.title: No Cost Unless You Recover
items.desc: We work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless your family receives a recovery. That lets grieving families focus on healing instead of worrying about legal bills.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California law gives priority to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children. If none of those exist, certain other dependents or heirs may be eligible to bring the claim. We can review your family's specific situation to confirm who has standing.

items.question: How long do we have to file after a loved one passes away in Los Altos?
items.answer: Generally, California gives families two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. If a government entity, such as a public road authority connected to a corridor like Foothill Expwy or I-280, may be involved, the deadline is often much shorter. It's worth speaking with us early to avoid missing any cutoff.

items.question: What can a wrongful death claim actually cover?
items.answer: Recoverable losses typically include funeral and burial costs, the financial support the deceased would have provided, and the loss of companionship, love, and guidance. It does not involve any criminal charges, which are handled separately by the state. We can walk through which losses may apply to your family's circumstances.

items.question: Is there a charge to speak with you about our case?
items.answer: No. We provide a free consultation, and we work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. We do not guarantee any result.
